voiceover:
[conversational] A link-in-bio tool is making $3.5M a month, and it takes no cut.

[curious] Stay till the end, because one pricing move changed everything for them.

It's called Stan. Creators and coaches use it to sell courses, coaching calls, memberships and digital products from one mobile page.

[confident] These numbers are verified on TrustMRR. As of April 2026, that's $3.5M MRR, 101,590 active subscriptions, and $76.6M in all-time revenue.

How'd it grow? Co-founder John Hu posted career-advice TikToks, then built Stan in public. He said building an audience online was the entirety of his early success. And they've said they never spent a single dollar on paid ads.

So, what can you steal? One, build your audience where your customers already hang out. Two, turn your customers into your sales force.

[serious] Honest catch: there's no free plan. Creator is $29 a month, and TrustMRR shows revenue, not profit.

[whispers] Now, the pricing move. Around $1M in revenue, they removed transaction fees and went flat monthly. Co-founder Vitalii Dodonov says revenue grew 8.5x the next year.

[playful] Would you pay $29 a month for a page like this? Send this to the friend who keeps saying they'll monetize their audience. Hack saved?

topic: Business breakdown: Stan — Stan enables people to make living and work for themselves.

pick.topic: Business breakdown: Stan — Stan enables people to make living and work for themselves.
pick.angle: A creator-economy platform that has made $3.5M, helping people turn their audience into a business

research.what_it_does: A link-in-bio storefront where creators sell digital products, courses, coaching calls, memberships and bookings from one mobile-first page, with no separate website.
research.who_pays: Creators, coaches and solo entrepreneurs (mostly social-first) pay a flat monthly subscription. Stan takes no cut of their sales.
research.pricing: No free plan, but a 14-day free trial on both plans. Creator is $29/mo or $300/yr. Creator Pro is $99/mo or $948/yr. Stan charges 0% transaction fees. Stripe/PayPal processing still applies (about 2.9% + $0.30 per US card payment). Source: Stan's help center and pricing article, as cited by third-party reviews checked Oct–Nov 2026 (checkoutpage.com, lilachbullock.com). I could not open the official pricing page directly.
growth: Founder-led content on TikTok and YouTube. Co-founder/CEO John Hu (@jayhoovy) posted career-advice TikToks while a Stanford GSB student, then built Stan in public. In the Creator Spotlight podcast (Dec 2024) he said that early on 'the entirety of my success was due to building an audience online'. He also estimated about 60% of his mental energy went into content for the first one or two years. (creatorspotlight.com, marketingcrafted.com)

Customers as salespeople. Hu told Forerunner Ventures that Stan aligns incentives with a profit share so customers act as affiliates, and that Stan hasn't spent a single dollar on paid ads. (forerunnerventures.com)
Sacra reports a 20% lifetime revenue-share affiliate program, plus word of mouth on TikTok and Instagram. This is a third-party report, not Stan's own statement. (sacra.com)

Pricing change: in late 2022, at roughly $1M annual revenue, the founders removed transaction fees and moved to a flat monthly subscription. Per the Mike Wystrach podcast page, revenue grew 8.5x over the following year. (mikewystrach.com)
Stan launched in May 2021 and by the end of 2022 was doing over $1M ARR. (thezerotoone.co)
Stan's own 2024 review says revenue went from $1.7M in 2022 to $14.7M in 2023 to over $33M in 2024. (stan.store/blog/creator-economy-2024)
Partnership: on Sep 15, 2025 Stan announced Gary Vaynerchuk as a partner and investor, tied to a creator challenge. The release described 80,000+ creators and $300M in sales. (PR Newswire)
Launched an AI content tool, Stanley, built in 14 days. Dodonov says it hit $50,000 MRR within six weeks. (AOL/Business Insider-style first-person article)
founder_story: Stan has two co-founders: John Hu (CEO, the creator/face of the brand) and Vitalii Dodonov (CTO, the engineer). TrustMRR lists only Dodonov. Dodonov describes meeting Hu through a shared customer. In his own X post he says he met his co-founder on Zoom in 2021 during COVID. (mikewystrach.com, X)
Dodonov started at Deloitte, then eBay. He quit eBay to work on Stan full-time in June 2021. (AOL article)
Dodonov moved to Canada at 18 without speaking English. He grew up in a small town in Russia, where his dad was a 10-time skydiving world champion. (Dodonov's X post, Feb 25, 2026)
Hu previously worked at Goldman Sachs and went to Stanford GSB. He built Stan to monetize his own TikTok following. (marketingcrafted.com, forerunnerventures.com)
Dodonov says Stan hit about $30M ARR in three years. He also says it did so with a small team: 'less than 30 people' and about 10 engineers (his own X posts, Jan 2026).
Hu and Dodonov raised $5M in seed funding from Forerunner in 2022. Dodonov's X thread says they returned an IKEA table 'with $5M in the bank'. (thezerotoone.co, X)
lessons: Build an audience where your customers already are. Hu documented the company on TikTok and YouTube to reach creators, and said that was the entirety of his early success.
Make your customers your sales force. Stan pays affiliates a share, has said it spends nothing on paid ads, and its customers' own 'Try 14 Days Free' banner works as a built-in referral.

Pick a simple, flat pricing model that works as the pitch. Stan dropped transaction fees at about $1M revenue. Advisors told them they were leaving millions on the table. Dodonov says revenue grew 8.5x in the next year.
Delete work rather than add it. Dodonov says Stan automated and simplified, 'deleting features' and building self-serve tools, to run lean.
Borrow credibility from bigger names. The Gary Vaynerchuk investment and partnership gave Stan an audience and a creator challenge to point at.
criticism: Revenue is not profit. TrustMRR shows MRR and revenue only, not margins. Dodonov has called Stan a 'profitable company', and Sacra claims about 40% EBITDA, but neither is verified.
TrustMRR's Stripe key has expired, so the figures stop at Apr 20, 2026 and may be stale. Stan's founders post different MRR figures at different times: $2.5M in Feb 2026 and $2.8M in Jan 2026.

Stan has a paid-only model with no free plan, which is costly for creators with no audience yet. Reviewers note it only pays off once sales clear roughly $290–$300/month. (creatorstackclub.com, elev8or.io)

Stan lacks a custom domain on the Creator plan, and removing the Stan branding needs Creator Pro. Stripe/PayPal fees and cash-out fees still apply, so 'zero fees' only means Stan's own fees. (cartmango.com, checkoutpage.com)

Competition is heavy. It is a link-in-bio and course-store market with Linktree, Beacons, Whop, Kajabi and others. Stan is also not a fit for megastar creators, and Hu says it is not designed for them. (entrepreneur.com)
Stan is VC-backed. It has Forerunner seed money, Steven Bartlett reported as a co-owner since May 2025, and Gary Vaynerchuk as an investor since Sep 2025. It is not purely bootstrapped.
facts: TrustMRR: MRR $3,569,654, all-time revenue $76,627,685, 101,590 active subscriptions, rank #3. The data was last updated Apr 20, 2026.
Stan says it serves 80,000+ creators making $200M+ per year on the platform. (Dodonov's X post)
Stan's own blog says it has helped creators earn over $400 million. A Mike Wystrach page for Dodonov says over $600M. (stan.store blog, mikewystrach.com)
11,000+ creators have earned their first $1,000 using Stan. (Stan 2024 review)
On Mar 17, 2026, Stan launched Stanley, an AI head of content for LinkedIn. (PR Newswire, via Tracxn)
Dodonov grew his LinkedIn from 1,724 followers to over 8,600 in 1.5 years by posting consistently. (stan.store/blog/by-creators-for-creators)
do_not_claim: Profit or margins. 'Profitable' is a founder claim, and 'about 40% EBITDA' comes from Sacra, with no verified financials.
Exact team size. Dodonov says under 30 people, while Latka lists 171, which looks unreliable.
That Dodonov is the sole founder, or that Stan was founded in April 2023. TrustMRR says April 2023, but sources say 2020 (founded) and May 2021 (launch).

Any funding or valuation figures from Tracxn, CB Insights, Clay, TechCrunch or Caplight. They mix up Stan Store with STAN, an unrelated Indian gaming app that raised from Google, Square Enix and others.
Exact valuation. The $25M valuation figure on the $5M seed round is only from thezerotoone.co.
Exact ARR or MRR on a given date. Sources quoted $27M, $30M, $33M and $2.5M–$2.8M MRR at different times.
Affiliate payout terms as an official fact. The 20% lifetime share comes from Sacra, not Stan.
research.notes: 1) Founder mismatch: TrustMRR lists Vitalii Dodonov (co-founder and CTO). The CEO and public face is John Hu (@jayhoovy). Credit both. 2) Pricing is cross-checked from many review sites that cite Stan's help center, and none showed the official pricing page text. Before recording, open stan.store and the pricing page yourself and confirm that '$29' and 'Creator Pro' appear. The pricing URL comes from a Heartbeat citation of Stan's own blog, and I haven't seen it live. 3) Beware name collision: most funding search results are for the Indian gaming app 'STAN' and not Stan Store. 4) TrustMRR data is stale (Apr 2026), so 'current MRR' should be phrased 'as of April 2026'. 5) The sources conflict on how much the 14-day trial matters. Stan's help center says the first month is charged when the trial ends, and the trial auto-converts unless cancelled before day 14.
